# Directive (EU) 2023/2673 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 November 2023

amending Directive 2011/83/EU as regards financial services contracts concluded at a distance and repealing Directive 2002/65/EC

## Article 1 — Amendments to Directive 2011/83/EU

(4) the following Article is inserted:

### Article 11a — Exercise of the right of withdrawal for contracts concluded by means of an online interface

1. In the case of contracts concluded by means of an online interface, the trader shall ensure that the consumer can also exercise the right of withdrawal by means of a withdrawal function. The withdrawal function shall be labelled with the words 'withdraw contract here' or a corresponding unambiguous formulation in an easily legible manner. The withdrawal function shall be continuously available during the withdrawal period. It shall be prominently displayed on the online interface and easily accessible to the consumer.

2. The withdrawal function shall allow the consumer to send an online withdrawal statement informing the trader of the consumer's decision to withdraw from the contract. That online withdrawal statement shall allow the consumer to provide or confirm easily the following information:

(a) the consumer's name;

(b) details identifying the contract from which the consumer wants to withdraw;

(c) details of the electronic means by which the confirmation of withdrawal is to be sent to the consumer.

3. Once the consumer has filled in the online withdrawal statement in accordance with paragraph 2, the trader shall enable the consumer to submit it by means of a confirmation function. That confirmation function shall be labelled in an easily legible manner only with the words 'confirm withdrawal' or a corresponding unambiguous formulation.

4. When the consumer submits the online withdrawal statement, the trader shall communicate to the consumer without undue delay an acknowledgement of receipt of the withdrawal on a durable medium, including its content and the date and time of submission.

5. The consumer shall be deemed to have exercised the right of withdrawal within the relevant withdrawal period if the consumer submitted the online withdrawal statement referred to in this Article before that period has expired.

## Article 2 — Transposition

1. Member States shall adopt and publish, by 19 December 2025, the measures necessary to comply with this Directive. They shall apply those measures from 19 June 2026.

# Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 31 May 2023

on the making available on the Union market and the export from the Union of certain commodities and products associated with deforestation and forest degradation and repealing Regulation (EU) No 995/2010

## Article 1 — Subject matter and scope

1. This Regulation lays down rules regarding the placing and making available on the Union market, as well as the export from the Union, of relevant products, as listed in Annex I, that contain, have been fed with or have been made using relevant commodities, namely cattle, cocoa, coffee, oil palm, rubber, soya and wood.

## Article 3 — Prohibition

Relevant commodities and relevant products shall not be placed or made available on the market or exported, unless all the following conditions are fulfilled: (a) they are deforestation-free; (b) they have been produced in accordance with the relevant legislation of the country of production; and (c) they are covered by a due diligence statement.

## Article 4 — Obligations of operators

1. Operators shall exercise due diligence in accordance with Article 8 prior to placing relevant products on the market or exporting them in order to demonstrate that the relevant products comply with Article 3.

2. Operators shall, prior to placing the relevant products on the market or exporting them, make available to the competent authorities via the information system referred to in Article 33 a due diligence statement confirming that due diligence was exercised and that no or only a negligible risk was found.

## Article 9 — Information requirements

1. Operators shall collect information, documents and data demonstrating that the relevant products comply with Article 3. For this purpose, the operator shall collect, organise and keep for 5 years the following information relating to each relevant product, accompanied by evidence:

(d) the geolocation of all plots of land where the relevant commodities that the relevant product contains, or has been made using, were produced, as well as the date or time range of production;

## Article 31 — Record keeping

Operators shall keep for at least 5 years from the date of the placing on the market or export of the relevant products all documentation related to due diligence, in particular the due diligence statement, and shall make it available to the competent authorities upon request.

## Article 38 — Entry into force and application

Articles 3 to 13 shall apply from 30 December 2025; for operators that by 31 December 2020 were established as micro-undertakings or small undertakings they shall apply from 30 June 2026.
